title: NBA disburses Rs. 13.76 Crore  in ABS Funds across 28 States and 4 UTs: Linking Commercial Utilisation of Medicinal Plants with Biodiversity Conservation
body_text: The National Biodiversity Authority (NBA) has disbursed Rs. 13.76 crore to promote biodiversity conservation and sustainable use of biological resources across 28 States and 4 Union Territories. The allocation forms part of the Access and Benefit Sharing (ABS) contributions received from AYUSH products manufacturing companies for the commercial utilisation of medicinal plants and other plant-based biological resources. These contributions pertain to three applications involving the utilisation of a total of 234 plant species. These biological resources were procured through market and trader networks, making it difficult to identify the individual benefit claimers associated with their supply chains. However, considering the majority of the medicinal plants used by companies are from forest areas, the State forest cover and occurrence of medicinal plants in the State/UT are taken into account for disbursing the benefit-sharing amount. Among the 234 plant species, ten species, namely Guggul, Ashwagandha, Bhringraj, Punarnava, Sarpagandha, Kalmegh, Black Pepper, Indian Gooseberry, Gokhura and Shalparni, contributes for a benefit-sharing amount of Rs. 6.45 Crore, out of Rs. 13.76 Crore. The ABS mechanism provides a means to channel the monetary benefits arising from their commercial utilisation towards biodiversity conservation, sustainable harvesting and promoting cultivation of these valuable biological resources. The top 15 States with ABS allocation, besides others, are given below: S. No. SBB / UTBC Amount released (Rs.) 1 Maharashtra 1,75,24,129.00 2 Arunachal Pradesh 93,74,889.00 3 Andhra Pradesh 88,07,925.00 4 Karnataka 87,14,794.00 5 Kerala 79,30,040.00 6 Odisha 78,54,924.00 7 Madhya Pradesh 69,90,463.00 8 Tamil Nadu 63,03,300.00 9 Jharkhand 56,77,312.00 10 Rajasthan 52,75,096.00 11 Chhattisgarh 52,21,105.00 12 Gujarat 48,16,750.00 13 Assam 46,83,668.00 14 West Bengal 42,65,005.00 15 Himachal Pradesh 40,81,731.00 16 Others 3,00,80,041.00 Total 13,76,01,172.00 The funds transferred can support strengthening of local biodiversity governance, Biodiversity Management Committees (BMCs), updating People’s Biodiversity Registers, documentation of biological resources and associated traditional knowledge, research and capacity building, community-led conservation, restoration of degraded ecosystems, sustainable harvesting and cultivation practices, and biodiversity-based livelihood initiatives. The NBA has so far collected Rs. 278 crore through the ABS mechanism, of which around Rs. 218.86 crore has been disbursed towards biodiversity conservation and benefit-sharing initiatives across the country. India’s ABS framework contributes to the global biodiversity agenda and the implementation of the Kunming–Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (KMGBF). The Yerevan Pathway, adopted at CBD COP 17 (19–30 October 2026), emphasises resource mobilisation, scientific and technical cooperation, and accelerated implementation of biodiversity targets. India’s ABS mechanism supports these priorities by advancing Target 13 of the KMGBF on fair and equitable benefit sharing from the utilisation of genetic resources and associated traditional knowledge. Medicinal plants are an integral part of India’s biological wealth, traditional healthcare systems and rural livelihoods. They support communities engaged in their collection, cultivation, processing and trade, while the associated traditional knowledge forms an important part of India’s cultural heritage. The growing commercial utilisation of medicinal plants underscores the need for responsible sourcing, sustainable harvesting and conservation of wild populations. The ABS mechanism facilitates benefit sharing from their utilisation, supporting biodiversity conservation, strengthening local institutions and promoting community-based livelihoods. These efforts complement Government initiatives such as the National AYUSH Mission, National Medicinal Plants Board programmes and Pradhan Mantri Van Dhan Yojana, which promote medicinal plant cultivation, value addition and livelihood generation. ***** VM/SK
